newsitem.title: USA: Pistons owner plans $40 mln race track in Detroit.
newsitem.headline: Pistons owner plans $40 mln race track in Detroit.

text.p: The owner of the Detroit Pistons basketball team said Thursday he plans to build a $40 million to $45 million auto race track on an 80-acre section of the Michigan State Fairgrounds in Detroit.

William Davidson, who owns the Pistons, Palace Sports and Entertainment and glass manufacturer Guardian Industries Corp, said the one-mile oval Motor City Speedway will open in 1998 and will be financed entirely from private sources.
Construction of the 30,000-seat facility will begin in April of 1997 an the east side of the state fairgrounds and racing will begin the following April.
Palace Sports and Entertainment will lease the property from the state of Michigan and will share proceeds from races, concerts and other events with the state.
Gov. John Engler told a news conference that the facility will increase the fair's attendance and will generate millions of dollars for improvements to the fairgrounds.
Palace Sports and Entertainment said a full schedule of 12 race weekends is planned for the summer of 1998, which it called the busiest race card of any first year track.

The one-mile oval raceway will be able to host Indy car, stock car, truck, motorcycle and sprint car races, among others. Officials also said seating capacity can be expanded as auto racing's popularity grows.
"When we open the raceway in 1998, Detroit -- the automobile capital -- will be the only major city to have a facility of this nature within its limits," Davidson said.

The track is not expected to change plans for the annual Detroit Grand Prix Indy car race, sponsored by ITT Automotive, a unit of ITT Industries Inc. But it will compete with facilites controlled by another Detroit-based motor racing mogul, Roger Penske. Penske Motorsports Inc owns Michigan International Speedway, in Brooklyn, Mich., and is building a new track in Fontana Calif.
